The '''2001–02 Serie A''' (known as the [[Serie A]] [[Telecom Italia Mobile|TIM]] for sponsorship reasons) was the 100th season of top-tier Italian [[association football|football]], the 70th in a [[round-robin tournament]]. It was composed by 18 teams, for the 14th consecutive time from season 1988–89.

The first two teams qualified directly to the [[UEFA Champions League]], teams ending in the third and fourth places had to play [[UEFA Champions League|Champions League]] qualifications, teams ending in the fifth and sixth places qualified for the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] (another spot was given to the winner of [[Coppa Italia]]), while the last four teams were to be relegated to [[Serie B]]. However, [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]]'s subsequent bankruptcy led to them being placed in the fourth tier of Italian football.

[[Juventus FC|Juventus]] won its 26th title on the final day of the season after original leaders [[Inter Milan|Internazionale]] (who finished third) lost 4–2 away to [[S.S. Lazio|Lazio]], and with it their chance at winning their first ''Scudetto'' since 1989. Second place went to [[A.S. Roma|Roma]].

This season also featured [[A.C. Chievo Verona|Chievo]]'s "miracle". The club, newly promoted to Serie A for the first time, were top of the table for six weeks early in the season. However, after the Christmas break, they hit some bad form and finished the season in fifth place.

Eighteen teams competed in the league, with four promoted teams from [[2000–01 Serie B|Serie B]], [[Torino F.C.|Torino]], [[Piacenza Calcio|Piacenza]], [[AC ChievoVerona|Chievo]] and [[A.C. Venezia|Venezia]], replacing the four relegated teams from the [[2000–01 Serie A]] season, [[Reggina Calcio|Reggina]], [[Vicenza Calcio|Vicenza]], [[SSC Napoli|Napoli]] and [[AS Bari|Bari]].

*Fewest goals scored – [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] (29)
*Most goals conceded – [[ACF Fiorentina|Fiorentina]] (63)
